chapter: A Prayer for Blessings, Told to Crested Peaks

quests.title: Threadlike Whispers

dialogue.t: Hello again! Back for more tea? I can put on another pot.
About "Blazegem Inscriptions"...
Oh? You'd like to know about their... technical details?
As you're friends of Xilonen, I'm willing to share that information with you, yes... Let me pick something simple to start with.
They... Are actually accidental byproducts from my first time forging an Ancient Name.
Then, I accidentally made a mistake with the Phlogiston Engraving of an Ancient Name, creating some kind of "deviation" in the functionality of the Ancient Name.
It could not guide the "memories" and "emotions" that people feel, but rather it could take certain "memories" within itself.

At first, I thought it was utterly useless, so I tossed it in with the other defective products. But after Nechca fell ill, I suddenly thought of this "defective" Ancient Name... which is now known as a "Blazegem Inscription."
...Nechca lost her memories of the "past." But that past was clearly real... and there are many witnesses to those events.
I can use that Blazegem Inscription to extract memories related to Nechca from the witnesses.
And then, by gathering all those memories together, create an entire "memory bank" about Nechca's past for her.
That way... My little Nechca can come home. She'll remember... that Mama will always be by her side.
About your health...
I do apologize for making you worry, but... It's just as I said. I could collapse at any moment.
In order to forge "Ancient Names," I have paid a high price... Or perhaps I should say, I have given everything I can give, even my little Nechca.
I'm not bitter towards anyone, nor do I expect anything in return... Right now, all I want is to help Nechca get better.
And for that, I will offer everything I have and am.
See you later.
Goodbye. The roads outside are tough going, so please be careful.
Xilonen! Good thing you're here, I'm wondering if I can—
The shelf on the left, second row down, first axe on the right... that one's yours. The garden hoe belongs to Iknal and the hammer is Pacal's, so make sure you take the one that's yours.
I haven't even said why I'm here... But looks like you're about to head out for a break?
Yes, but I'm going to take it right here. The temperature's just perfect today.
Really? But doesn't it feel a lot hotter than usual? I really don't want to stay out in this heat.
Exactly. In hot weather like this, customers don't tend to stick around and talk when they're coming to place orders or pick up the goods.
I see... Oh, here comes another customer. I'll just leave you to it then, and pick up my axe.
Sure, sounds good to me.
Hey, Xilonen!
{NICKNAME}, Paimon, we meet again. You two seem to be in good spirits.
How's your Pilgrim's Chronicle been? Run into any issues?
No, everything is fine.
Good. It was also my first time receiving a Pilgrim's Chronicle. Even though I've already turned it over to you...
There are still a lot of things that could go wrong, so I wasn't sure if there would be any issues.
Huh? So, uh... what are the chances that something might still go wrong?
Less than the chances of Mualani accidentally falling off a Spiritway, I'd say.
Oh, well that definitely would never happen...
I've found the axe, Xilonen. Thanks a lot.
By the way, Nechca's birthday is coming up real soon. Are you planning to visit her?
I've prepared a gift, and was just getting ready to take it to her.
*sigh* You're not planning on giving the kid a full set of pliers again, are you? Or lemme guess, woodworking tools?

dialogue.sit: You'd give these kinds of things as... birthday gifts?
I'd like a set, too! Where can I buy one?

dialogue.t: That's right. Flowers will wither, toys will break, and snacks are quickly forgotten once they're eaten...
But a set of durable work tools will always stay with you, and get you through many sticky situations.
Still, I won't be giving Nechca any tools this year. She wrote me a letter saying that she'd like a copy of "Tequil the Brave."

The book is not what you'd call a bestseller, but luckily, I have a few copies in my collection. They were really old editions that were published a long time ago, but they should still be readable...
Haha, children her age love fairy tales. The last time I was at Tlazolli's, I even brought Nechca a—
Huh? Wait... what did I bring her again? It must have been her favorite thing, but... Uh... Why can't I remember it anymore?
It is quite hot today, seems you're about to pass out from the heat. Do you even remember your own name?
My memory can't be this bad. It's just these last few days... *sigh* I've been forgetting things for some odd reason.
In that case, why don't you use the Blazegem Inscription you have as a memo to engrave some important things to remember?
After all, that Inscription will never wear out, and it's easy to carry... I'd say that's quite a fitting use for it.
Ahem... You do have a point, but... my Inscription is almost already full.

dialogue.sit: Your name is that long?
Did you include all your relatives' names too?

dialogue.t: No, no. I engraved some wishes on my Blazegem Inscription.
You know, just some dreams that I have for the future and things I'd like to accomplish one day.
Even though Tlazolli has said that from an aesthetic point of view, it would be best for people to keep their Inscriptions short...
This Blazegem Inscription was still made by a Name Engraver, the forger of Ancient Names themselves.
Everyone thinks that the Inscriptions she made might have some... wondrous powers.
So, many people who bought Blazegem Inscriptions engraved their wishes and dreams on them in hopes that they would come true.
Sounds kinda like a Wish Granter...
But if you do that, won't everyone be able to see your wishes and dreams?

dialogue.sit: I was just wondering the same thing...
Yeah, that could be a little embarrassing...

dialogue.t: Hahaha, don't worry. We usually ask Tlazolli to add the inscriptions for us. She has a unique method of engraving.
With her method, the light must be at a certain angle in order to see the text.
Without the right angle of lighting, the Blazegem Inscription will just look like a pretty stone.
That's true. In the end, a Blazegem Inscription is essentially just a piece of rock. It doesn't have the power to grant people's wishes.
Making wishes to it is like shouting into an echoing valley — the only one who'll answer is yourself.
But... using it as a journal for your wishes is also fine. Carrying them with you and taking a look from time to time can be a good source of encouragement...
As long as you don't suddenly change your mind and want to take your wishes back, that is. These things are extremely durable — it would take a lot of effort to change the words.
And I don't think anyone would willingly part with it, either. They're not cheap, and very hard to get. If you ever lost it, you'd just be filled with regret.
Still, it's really strange... given Auntie's skill, how could it take so long for her to make one? I hope someone didn't give her the idea of making fewer and selling for more.

dialogue.sit: Ugh, I know just the person who would do that...
Sounds just like one of Cheven's schemes...

dialogue.t: Hahaha! It's true, Cheven could totally have put that in her ear. Still, I don't think it's a bad thing for Tlazolli to make some money by selling these.
At least she and little Nechca are better off now, and won't have to worry about the cost of treating her illness anymore.
I was really worried about their family at first, and was even planning to send them some... uh, send some...
Huh? What was I planning to send to Nechca again? Ugh, this memory of mine...
Alright. If you stay out in the heat for any longer, I'm afraid even the Inscription won't be able to save your memory. You should go back and get some rest.
Right... Right. Please give my regards to Tlazolli and Nechca.
What's going on? Maybe I should go talk to Erinle to get some medicine...
So you'll be going to Nechca's birthday party, too, Xilonen? Ooh, perfect, then let's go together!
Sure, but I didn't expect you to know Tlazolli, too. She hasn't even been coming to the tribe much lately, so how did you get a chance to talk with her?
Sounds just like one of Cheven's schemes...
Yeah, that could be a little embarrassing...
Did you include all your relatives' names too?
I'd like a set, too! Where can I buy one?
I make these myself, and it's a lot of work. But if you'd like a set, I can make some time and forge one for you.
Great! We often camp out in the wild, but a set of Xilonen's tools would make pitching a tent and starting a bonfire a whole lot easier.
Xilonen! Good thing you're here, I'm wondering if I can—
The shelf on the left, second row down, first axe on the right... that one's yours. The garden hoe belongs to Iknal and the hammer is Pacal's, so make sure you take the one that's yours.

I see... Oh, here comes another customer. I'll just leave you to it then, and pick up my ax.
Sure, sounds good to me.
Hey, Xilonen!
{NICKNAME}, Paimon, we meet again. You two seem to be in good spirits.
How's your Ancient Name been? Run into any issues?
No, everything is fine.
Good. It was my first time working with the Lord of the Night to forge an Ancient Name, and you're not even from Natlan.
There are still a lot of things that could go wrong, so I wasn't sure if there would be any issues.

Well, less than the chances of Mualani accidentally falling off a Spiritway, I'd say.

dialogue.sit: You explain your encounter with Tlazolli to Xilonen...

dialogue.t: So that's how you met her... She even wants to use Volcanic Crystal as a forging material... Guess she's really pulling out all the stops for her daughter.

dialogue.sit: We also wanted to get a gift for Nechca.
But we have no idea what she might like...

dialogue.t: Then let's just go and ask. Come on, I want to give her the book anyway.
Huh? Wait a second, aren't birthday gifts supposed to be a surprise?
If we ask Nechca, then she'll know what gift we'll be getting her, and that would ruin the surprise!
But if you don't ask her, then how will you know what kind of present she would like?
Here's another idea. Perhaps you can also give her a storybook based on what she wrote in her letter. That might be a good option.
Easy enough, I have loads of those in my bag.
But shouldn't we give it a little more thought? If we all give her books, it might seem like we didn't put much effort into it.
Xilonen, have you really never asked her what she would like the most? There must be something else she'd like besides books.

Unfortunately, no. Nechca's illness has kept flaring up over the past few years. Apparently, she couldn't do anything during that time other than rest in her bed. She didn't even have the strength to talk to anyone.
It wasn't until recently that she started to recover from her illness and regained the strength to write letters to others.
Anyway, there's no need to overthink it. Worst case scenario, I can split the book into two volumes and we can each give her one.

dialogue.sit: Great idea!
Let's just go and ask Nechca.

dialogue.t: No, that's terrible! That would really look like we didn't try!
Let's just go ask Nechca. Even though it would ruin the surprise, we could at least get her something that would make her happy.
Anyway, could you tell us a bit more about the book that you're getting her? Is it really that unpopular?
It's a little difficult to explain. You see, there are actually two versions of "Tequil the Brave."
The premise of the book is pretty straightforward. It's basically about a set of twin brothers working to defeat a demon lord.
But after defeating the demon lord, the older brother Tequil discovers that king's spirit has possessed his younger brother, Rimac.
In the ending of the original story, the older brother kills his younger brother to defeat the demon lord, before himself jumping into a volcano.
I remember there was one line that was super popular at the time. If I still remember right, after being possessed by the Goddess Coatlicue, Rimac said...
"I do not wish to see your blood be reduced to ash, but I have seen the light of your heart and spirit. Remember my name, brother. As long as you remember me, I will never have left."
So what about the other version of the story?
The other version was released only recently. The author heard a suggestion from someone and suddenly decided to try and make a stake in the fairy tale market, so the story was revised...
In the revised version, the brothers killed the demon lord together and both survived. According to the author, this gave the story a happy-ever-after kind of ending.
However, the revised version was not well-received... After a month on the market, it had hardly sold any copies, and the books were collecting dust on the store shelves.
The store owners desperately tried to get rid of the book, and have resorted to all sorts of promotions and discounts to sell it.
Even now, the only edition of Tequil the Brave you can find on the market is the newer one, whereas the older edition is nearly impossible to find.
Anyway, I couldn't bring myself to give such a poorly-rated book to Nechca... So I spent a few days looking, and managed to find a few copies of the old edition in a warehouse.
I picked out a copy that looked relatively new, and wrapped it up as a present for Nechca.
If you're interested, I can give you this extra copy to read. The pages are pretty old, though, so please be gentle with it.
Oh, and here's a copy of the newer edition, too. They gave me a free copy when I went to buy some Xocoatl.
So that's how they're trying to sell off the book... could it really be that bad? Even Paimon's curious now.

dialogue.sit: That's two more for the collection.
You can read them to me while we're on the road, Paimon.

dialogue.t: Let's get going. Tlazolli lives pretty far from the tribe, so it'll take us some time to get there.
You can read them to me while we're on the road, Paimon.
Okay, but you'll have to carry Paimon for a while. Once Paimon's done reading it herself, she'll read it out for you.
Let's just go and ask Nechca.
Yeah, even though it would ruin the surprise, we could at least get her something that would make her happy.
But we have no idea what she might like...
Go on now, Iengu. Nechca is still resting.
*whine*
Hey Tlazolli, we're here!
Oh? What a surprise! And even Xilonen is here, too...
We came to visit Nechca.
It's been a while since I've seen you last, Auntie.
I received Nechca's letter. She wanted a copy of Tequil the Brave, right? I've brought the book for her.
There are several editions of the book in Natlan, and I wasn't sure which version she'd prefer.
I asked a messenger from the Scions of the Canopy. It seems this softcover edition is one of the most popular options, so I bought it for Nechca.
Heh, you haven't changed a bit, Xilonen.
Let's go inside. I was just boiling some Xocoatl, so you can all try some.
Xilonen used to love drinking Xocoatl. When she was little, she would always have several cups every time she came to visit me.
You were already a big girl by the time I finally had my Nechca. Alright, for now, let's—
Oof...!
Auntie...? Let's go inside.
{NICKNAME}, please help me get her into the house.
Sure thing!
Oh, Paimon will help, too!
Be good, Iengu, and don't get in the way!
*whine*!
Alright, let's get indoors. Watch your step now, Auntie.
Sorry, Nechca's illness has been flaring up recently, so I was up for a few nights.
I suddenly started to feel dizzy in the sun... I hope I didn't scare you.
Have a seat. I'll fetch you a few cups of Xocoatl. Please wait a moment...
I've already brought them over. This cup's for you, Aunt Tlazolli. And these are for you two.
Xocoatl... What does it taste like? Paimon's heard that it can be pretty bitter... {NICKNAME}, could you give it a try first?
Don't worry, Auntie always adds lots of sugar. It won't be bitter.
The last time you came to visit, you were still just a kid. But now you're a pillar of the Children of Echoes... No, of all Natlan even!
It's all thanks to the drinks I had here, and the books I happened to read.
You've been close for quite some time, then?
We heard that you two are from the same tribe... but Paimon had no idea you were so close.
When I was little, my parents were always talking about how skilled Auntie was at forging Ancient Names, and how she was such a good role model for all the rest of us...
The moment I became idle at home, they would toss me into Auntie's workshop to watch and learn...
Then your parents would go back, I would boil you a pot of Xocoatl, and let you play in the house.
Yeah. Then I would drink, and listen to you banging away with your tools in the workshop.
But eventually, she moved out of the tribe to find some more space for her workshop, and I didn't have the chance to visit again after that.
But why did you seem so familiar with the place when you went to the kitchen for the drinks just now?
Because the layout of this place is identical to her old house.
Let me see... Ah, that should be Nechca's bedroom, then?
That's right. Hehe, I remember you used to hunker down in the room to read and draw...
But you're all grown up now... Even if you wanted to live here, I'm afraid you've already outgrown Nechca's bed.

dialogue.sit: You two seem like family.
Xilonen seems just like an older sister to Nechca.

dialogue.t: That's how Nechca sees Xilonen, too. Whenever she's feeling better, she always asks me when her penpal sister would be coming to visit.
Well, I'm here now, and even brought a gift as an apology. I'll leave the book here.

You said Nechca asked you for the book? I hope it wasn't too much trouble to get... Really, I'm surprised that she even asked you for a present. When she's at home, she'd even ask me for permission to eat some snacks.
*sigh* Maybe I've been too strict with her. She's obviously starting to like her big sister more than her own mother!
Really? Well, I'd say I really haven't done enough to deserve the title of big sister.
I wasn't able to help her when she was sick, and I didn't even come and properly visit her that many times. The only thing I've been able to do is to help her find some books.
Don't be too hard on yourself, Xilonen. You have great responsibilities as the Name Engraver of the tribe. We both know you are far too busy to take care of her.
The responsibilities on your shoulders also became far heavier when I... gave up on my work.
You just had more important things to tend to, Auntie... No one in the tribe blames you. We all know that Nechca needs her mother's care.
But that doesn't change the fact that I gave up on my work. And... even now, I still have not found the courage to pick up my hammer again.
I'm sorry to leave you to shoulder all the responsibilities alone, Xilonen.
Whoa, why so somber all of a sudden... Uh, don't be so sad, everyone! Hasn't Nechca gotten better lately?
Relax, Auntie. I can handle the work. But once Nechca is back on her feet, you should get back to work and let me have a vacation.
You'll be the one who's busy then, and I'll be sitting at the side drinking Xocoatl and cheering you on.
Heh, if that day really comes, you can have as much Xocoatl as you like.

dialogue.sit: So how did Nechca get so sick?
Is her condition really that serious?

dialogue.t: Hehe... If you asked me before, I wouldn't have even been able to talk about it.
But now that she's gradually recovering... I've also gained some courage to face what happened back then.
Nechca's illness actually originates from the Abyss.
That night, I was in the tribe, having a discussion over the forging of new Ancient Names.
Before we could finish our discussion, the alarm started to ring outside. A horde of monsters from the Abyss suddenly attacked the tribe, so everyone banded together to fight them off.
I joined the fray as well, and it wasn't until the monsters were repelled that I got back home with some guards from the tribe... But Nechca was gone.
I can't remember how long I spent searching for her... Maybe for two or three days... In the end, we found Nechca at the bottom of a short cliff.
She was holding a dried-up Embercore Flower in her hand, and there were traces of Abyssal corruption around her wounds.
I know... it was all my fault. Before the incident, Nechca had asked if I could forge an Ancient Name for her.
Work was busy at the time, so I told her that if she could find an Embercore Flower, I would use it as material to forge her an Ancient Name.
Oh Nechca, my daughter... My Nechca... I was holding her in my arms, but no matter how many times I called her name, she wouldn't open her eyes and look at me...
I was the one who decided to move my workshop to the outskirts of our tribe for work... and I was the one who left her home alone.
Oh... *sobs* My daughter, my Nechca... Why do you have to suffer like this? *sobs*
Whoa...! Hey, hey... It's okay, right? Nechca's getting better!
She already has the strength to write letters now, doesn't she? We... Uh well, Xilonen has even brought her a gift!

dialogue.sit: Please drink some water first.
Things will get better.

dialogue.t: Sorry, I just can't control myself whenever I remember that time.
Phew, alright... it's not every day that we get guests. I really shouldn't be crying like this.
I asked someone to buy some ingredients for me, so why don't you stay for dinner tonight? I'll make some Shrimp Bisque, Grilled Fish in Mint Sauce, and Tower Tacos.
We'll help! That sounds like a lot to make, and we don't want you to tire yourself out.

dialogue.sit: Let me flex my cooking skills.
Enough talk, let's start with a fried egg!

dialogue.t: Hahaha! Thank you both. But don't worry, it's just a few dishes. I'll be fine.
You three just need to make sure everything gets eaten up. I can't eat a lot at this age.
Oh, we haven't had anything to eat yet, so don't worry! We'll make sure there are no leftovers!

dialogue.sit: I promise the plates will be picked clean!
I can eat an entire fish myself.

dialogue.t: Ah, it just occurred to me that Xilonen likes to eat Cheesy Crab Hotpot. Why don't I make that instead of the Grilled Fish in Mint Sauce? I remember you don't like picking out fish bones.
Both are fine with me. I've learned to just chew up the fish bones now.
Oh, c'mon now. If you don't want to pick out the bones, I can just take them out for you...
Anyway... for dessert, would you like a Cup O' Grainfruit or Chocolate?
Cup O' Grainfruit!
Chocolate!
How about a Cup O' Grainfruit mixed with Chocolate?
Okay, got it. I'll go start cooking, but could you do me a favor in the meantime?
I ordered a bunch of ingredients, and they should be here any minute now. Would you go check by the door and see if they were already here? If so, please bring them in.
C'mon Xilonen, stop lying around. You shouldn't nap before dinner, it'll ruin your appetite.
Hey! I'm not a kid anymore, you know. You don't have to worry about my appetite.
That's beside the point. If you don't watch out for your health while you're still young, then when you get older, you'll—
Alright, alright... I'm getting up!
We'll go check on the ingredients with Xilonen. It isn't far, so it shouldn't take us long.
*sigh* That kid...
I can eat an entire fish myself.
Enough talk, let's start with a fried egg!
Huh? She mentioned all those delicious dishes, and you're just going to make a fried egg!?
Things will get better.
Is her condition really that serious?
Xilonen seems just like an older sister to Nechca.
Hmm, no one's come to deliver the ingredients yet... Paimon thought we'd see someone come flying down on a Yumkasaur as soon as we came out.
A messenger from the Scions of the Canopy wouldn't be flying here. They usually come climbing down the cliffs nearby.
No need to look, there isn't anyone on the cliffs.

dialogue.sit: So should we keep walking?
Maybe the delivery person got lost?

dialogue.t: I—I just saw a ghost! *panting*
Hey, you there! Sorry, but does Tlazolli live around here?
Oh, are you the one who's supposed to deliver the ingredients?
I don't see any ingredients...
Ingredients? Are you kidding? I was nearly eaten myself!
Ugh, never mind that now. Those monsters are still hot on my heels! Please, you've gotta help me!
Xilonen, we... Huh? Where'd she go?
Whoa! She's already gone up to fight the monsters! Let's go help her out!
Maybe the delivery person got lost?
That kid... She's just like Nechca.
Seriously! Since when have there been so many monsters here?
Alright... That should be it for the monsters. Was easier than I thought.
It also seems we're in luck — the goods weren't damaged either.
Strange... we didn't see any monsters on the way here.

dialogue.sit: You must have terrible luck.
You didn't provoke them, did you?

dialogue.t: Yeah right! I use this road to deliver goods all the time, and I've never been attacked like this before.
It's the main road in and out of the tribe, so people often come here to clear out any monsters. This area's usually very safe.
I don't know what happened, but it seems like all the monsters around here have gone berserk. Even the docile Tepetlisaurs are in a frenzy!
*sigh* Tlazolli doesn't even forge Ancient Names anymore, so why can't she just move back to the tribe?
If she comes back, Nechca will even be able to find some playmates. She's so young, and hasn't even—
Uh... Nechca's playmates... No, wait. I feel like my kids have played with her before. They've even told me about Nechca's favorite game... If I remember right, it was...
Strange, I always remembered it before... How could I forget all of a sudden...?
Look at that! He has a Blazegem Inscription, too.

dialogue.sit: So luck shouldn't be the problem.
Seems there's quite a market for those Inscriptions...

dialogue.t: You should go back to the tribe — it seems like you had quite the scare today. We'll take the ingredients back for you.
I'll carry these bags, you two can carry the rest.

dialogue.sit: Sure thing.
Paimon can help, too.

dialogue.t: If you say so! Thank you so much. I guess today's just a really bad day for me to go outside...
That's so weird... Why is everyone we've run into today having trouble remembering stuff?
And they're all carrying Blazegem Inscriptions.
Paimon's not sure how to say it... but she's got a strange feeling about this. Like it's all somehow related...
Once you live long enough, you'll eventually start experiencing strange days like this.
Let's bring the ingredients back. Otherwise, we won't have anything to eat tonight.
Paimon can help, too.
Huh? Oh, sure... Uh, Paimon can take care of these Grainfruit that fell out of the bag!
Seems there's quite a market for those Inscriptions...
You didn't provoke them, did you?
Ah, you're finally back. What took you so long? I was starting to worry.
We ran into some small problems, but everything's fine now.
Alright, as long as everything's okay now. You all have a seat, I'll get the food ready. It won't take long.

dialogue.sit: Tlazolli gets to work on the food. After cooking for some time, delicious dishes are set on the table one after another...

dialogue.t: Whoa, there's so much tasty food! You're amazing, Tlazolli!
They were all pretty simple dishes to make. Don't be shy. Dig in, everyone!

dialogue.sit: What would you like to start with, Paimon?
No flying on the table, Paimon.

dialogue.t: Hehe, Paimon will help herself! Hmm, Paimon will have some of this, and this... oh, and this!
Can I get another serving, please?
Y—You're done already!? Do you even chew when you're eating!?
Of course. Didn't I say that I chew up the fish bones?
I'll have just one more fish, and leave the rest for Nechca.
It's okay, just go ahead and eat all you'd like. Nechca can't eat these dishes anyway.
Her body is too weak to digest these kinds of things. I'll just make some broth for her.
Oh no... But, Paimon thought she had already recovered from her illness.
Injuries caused by the Abyss cannot be undone. The doctor said the fact that she's stable is already quite a miracle.
But it's okay! Nechca can talk to me now, and can even hold my hand... That's more than I could ask for.
...Even if she will never again know that I am her mother.
Wh—What do you mean?
The doctor said the Abyss has had an irreversible effect on Nechca's soul. She... She's lost all her memories from before she was injured.
The doctor also said that this sort of memory loss isn't like simply forgetting something. Rather, she can no longer remember anything from before that fateful day.
Huh? But, how does that happen?
You know about the woven scrolls that the Masters of the Night-Wind use to record things, right?

Well, generally speaking, forgetting things is like when the woven scrolls would gradually start to fade. As long as you re-paint and weave the threads again, the faded memories will come back to life.
But the case of Nechca's memory loss is as if her woven scroll had been cut in two, and the portion from the past was burned to ashes.
The books she loved to read, the flowers she took joy to grow... and the time she spent in this house were all cut off by the Abyss, and can never be retrieved again.
As one example of that, Nechca now only sees me as... a strange, unfamiliar Auntie who claims to be her mother.
She's a good kid, and doesn't want to upset this lady who's been taking care of her so much, so she still calls me "Mom."
But I've always had a feeling that she's constantly wondering about things like... Where is her real mother? Why is she stuck here in this house? Was she abandoned?
Nechca really has no idea that her real mother is right in front of her, and has never left...
So, you plan on recreating Nechca's woven scroll all by yourself?
What do you mean?
Or should I say, you've already started reweaving that scroll long ago?

dialogue.sit: A Blazegem Inscription...
Whose is it?

dialogue.t: The delivery guy's. I saw it hanging from his waist, so I asked to borrow it from him.
Don't worry. I'll return the Inscription to him once we've figured everything out. These things aren't cheap, after all.
When did you know?
I noticed it back when Blazegem Inscriptions suddenly became popular among the tribe.
It was then that I also noticed that everyone wearing Blazegem Inscriptions had varying degrees of memory loss.
{NICKNAME}, you've picked up on it too, haven't you?

dialogue.sit: Everyone's memory loss...
Had something to do with Nechca.

dialogue.t: "Accessories made using Ancient Name forging techniques"... For what's only supposed to be a pretty souvenir, this Inscription contains a Phlogiston Engraving with a truly overkill level of complexity.
The shape and patterns of these engravings are also identical to that of an Ancient Name.
By making just a few slight adjustments to the layout and connections of the main pattern, you can pretty much qualify this Blazegem Inscription as a bona fide Ancient Name.
...And yet, you've never told anyone about these engravings in the Blazegem Inscriptions that can be activated at any time.
Am I right, Auntie?
...I always knew you were a sharp one, Xilonen.
That's right. I have a way to cure Nechca and restore all her memories. It's actually quite simple.
I want to forge an Ancient Name for Nechca that contains all of her past memories.

dialogue.sit: You're going to... make an Ancient Name for Nechca?
But Ancient Names must be approved by the Wayob...

dialogue.t: And the reason they must be approved by the Wayob is because the memories they bear are all stored within the Ley Lines.
Extracting those memories from the Ley Lines requires the Wayob's assistance.
But your plan wouldn't need you to do any of that, right, Auntie?
Your Blazegem Inscriptions will help you complete that part of your plan in the Ley Lines' place. You will use the Inscriptions to form a massive memory bank for Nechca.
And the Ancient Name you're trying to forge will be used to extract corresponding memories from the memory bank.
A memory bank? Wait, so the reason all those people were having trouble remembering stuff is because... the Blazegem Inscriptions took away any memories related to Nechca?

dialogue.sit: Even though Nechca has forgotten her own past...
Her life was still witnessed by other people...

dialogue.t: Using other people's memories of Nechca to reconstruct her past... This is the first time I've heard of such an idea.
You've seen through my plans, Xilonen. You're as outstanding as ever... far more brilliant than me.
I intend to use this method to collate all the memories related to Nechca, and allow her to regain her past again.
B—But, wouldn't extracting memories like that hurt the person carrying the Blazegem Inscription?
Not at all. Every time a Blazegem Inscription extracts memories, the process is under my precise control. That way, there's no chance of anyone in the tribe getting hurt.
This is the Central Inscription that controls all the other Blazegem Inscriptions...
...Which will also soon serve as Nechca's Ancient Name.
You made all this yourself, Tlazolli?

dialogue.sit: Even though it's not an official Ancient Name...
That's still a lot to do on your own...

dialogue.t: Yes, it was lots and lots of work... it was truly exhausting. Or perhaps... I've just grown old.
You saw it yourself, I nearly fainted just from being in the sun.
I could collapse tomorrow... or even in the next few moments, but Nechca's Ancient Name is still far from completion.
I've solved the issue of storing memories, but I still don't know how to connect Nechca up to this Central Inscription.
I thought you'd just modify your own Ancient Name.
I considered it, but this matter doesn't have anything to do with my Ancient Name.
It's of no help to me, and I don't need its help now.
You know the price to pay for making something like this.
Yes, I do. But as long as I can get my Nechca back, I'm willing to do whatever it takes.
Otherwise, Nechca won't have any chance of reclaiming her past once I'm dead and gone.
She won't remember me, and she won't even remember why her name is Nechca.
When that time comes, she would be left to drift around the world all alone... unknowing of where she came from, or where she should go.
She is my daughter, the one to whom I gave the Nechca name... Whether it be as her mother or as a Name Engraver, I can't simply stand by and let her name disappear.
Xilonen...

dialogue.sit: Shh, let her think about this for a moment.
Let her decide what to do.

dialogue.t: I'll take this Central Inscription with me.
I'm going to completely disassemble it to confirm its components and uses.
I won't make any promises until I've checked everything.
Say goodnight to Nechca for me, Auntie.
Oh... wait! I've also finished the Inscriptions for {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Let me fetch them for you.
I'm sorry it took me so long to finish them...
Hold on, Auntie.
{NICKNAME} and Paimon have never met Nechca before, so you can't draw any memories from them.
That wasn't my intention... They're just ordinary gifts. Please, take them...
Huh? What was that noise?
Nechca must have woken up and wants to get out of bed on her own... Sorry, I'll go check on her first.
Nechca! Don't try to get out of bed, just tell Mom if you need anything!
You go ahead and take care of Nechca, Auntie.
Let's go, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. There are a few things I want to tell you.
Let her decide what to do.
That's still a lot to do on your own...
Her life was still witnessed by other people...
But Ancient Names must be approved by the Wayob...
Had something to do with Nechca.
Whose is it?
No flying on the table, Paimon.
But Paimon can't reach that dish... Could you give Paimon some? C'mon, c'mon!

quests.description: The time you and Tlazolli agreed upon has almost arrived. You prepare to pay her a visit to check on the Blazegem Inscription’s progress.

quests.title: A Faint Signal Lingers

dialogue.t: You two can wait outside for a moment — I just need to go in and grab something. The workshop is a little messy, so unfortunately, I won't be able to show you around.

dialogue.sit: But I want to have a look!
A mess is what I like best!

dialogue.t: Uh, that's not really what I mean... It's not the mess that's really the problem.
It's just that the workshop is cluttered with way too much stuff... Books, files, and even ancient texts I got from Masters of the Night-Wind.
Everything's piled up to the ceiling. You probably won't know where to step once you're inside.

Kachina suffered quite an unfortunate series of events the last time she went inside... Ahem, I suppose it was my fault for being so focused on searching for information at the time that I forgot to lock the door...

After entering the workshop, she was shocked to find herself face-to-face with a massive woven scroll from the Masters of the Night-Wind. Then, she turned around, and knocked over a huge stack of forging blueprints.
She tried to step out of the way, but tripped on an poster tube that was behind her. And then, BOOM, the forging blueprints came crashing right onto her head.
Oh no...

dialogue.sit: That must've hurt!
W—Was Kachina okay?

dialogue.t: She's lucky I noticed in time. I found Kachina in a daze and managed to save her before an entire set of the History of the Children of Echoes was about to bury her... I then dragged her up to the second floor.
Ever since then, Kachina always waits outside the door, and doesn't dare take a step in whenever she comes to see me.

dialogue.sit: Are there really that many books inside?
I thought a workshop was supposed to be full of tools...

dialogue.t: Yeah, you're an artisan and craftswoman, after all. We thought there would be weapons and armor hanging all over the place.
But it seems more like a library than a workshop.
Well, my primary work is forging Ancient Names, which is much trickier than making swords and tools. Aside from the necessary craftsmanship, I also need to consult many ancient texts.
You probably already know that each Ancient Name represents a certain "spirit," behind which are countless related stories to support it.
In other words, the essence of an Ancient Name is the physical manifestation of a certain spiritual will.
And as a Name Engraver, when I'm working on a new Ancient Name, I'm not only trying to give it a physical shape...
But more importantly, I'm also trying to understand the spirit contained within the name.
And to do that, I have to collect as many related stories as possible, and read through them all.
But, as you might know, people tend to add a lot of... extraneous details when it comes to stories about themselves.
For stories that have been clearly exaggerated or altered, I must gather other related stories or information as cross-references...
This way, I can filter out all the absurd and exaggerated details, and restore the person's life to its true nature.
Only in true stories can you find the authentic spirit.
And this is the only way for the spirit to become an Ancient Name that matches its essence.
We've heard about the concept behind Ancient Names before, but after hearing you explain the details, Paimon can't help but think that Ancient Names are really powerful!
If only they could be even more powerful...
No matter how powerful Ancient Names could be, they would never be able to suddenly turn into a blade, or allow you to smash through an entire cliff in one punch.
It's just a form of spiritual power that's passed down from generation to generation. It doesn't have those kinds of physically tangible effects.
Um... Take your own names, for example.
From the moment you appeared in this world, some person had already prepared a blessing for you.
That person then condensed this "blessing" into your name, and gave it to you as a gift.
It may feel like the moment you received your name is already in the past, but it will always stay with you, and move with you into the future.
"Names are blessings for the future from people standing in the past." That's what Auntie once told me.
With this blessing, people will become more confident as they walk into their future... To put it another way, it's like having a lamp in your hand as you walk through the darkness of night.
Oh, Paimon gets that! If you're alone when you're walking in the dark, it's easy to get scared and tired quickly.
But if someone else is walking with you, then it won't be nearly as scary. And... well, you might still get tired, but it'll still be a whole lot better than walking alone.
{NICKNAME} always has Paimon by his(her) side though, so he(she)'ll never have to worry about that.
Oh, Paimon's sure many wish they could be in your shoes, {NICKNAME}.
Please, you're always the one to get tired when we're on the road.
P—Paimon's always flying! Of course it gets tiring... But we're getting off-topic! We can talk about that later...

dialogue.sit: Try not to fall asleep on me next time...
At least try not to eat so much...

dialogue.t: Anyway, this is what Tlazolli told me when I was training as a Name Engraver.
To be honest, I've only understood twenty percent of what she said at most. I've never been able to figure out the rest.
But doesn't that basically mean you don't get it!?
Well, that's not entirely true. Auntie and I have at least come to a consensus on the most important thing.
Ah, I'm sick of talking, we can talk about this more later. Please wait a moment while I grab my things.

dialogue.sit: Xilonen opens the door and walks into her workshop. Some unsettling crashing sounds come from the workshop, followed by some agonizing creaks and squeaks.
Eventually, Xilonen rushes out the door with a box in her arms. She then turns around and kicks the door closed, shutting the sound of dusty books falling to the ground inside...

dialogue.t: Did you hear a whole section of something collapse in there just now?
*coughs* It's fine, it's fine. It was just a bunch of very old Ancient Name records, I've already made copies of them.
I kept this set of Phlogiston Wedges in the back, so it wasn't easy to take out. I had to resort to brute force.
Come on, let's go disassemble the Central Inscription. It shouldn't take long.
At least try not to eat so much...
I thought a workshop was supposed to be full of tools...
W—Was Kachina okay?
A mess is what I like best!
Nechca is finally better. Phew... I hope this is over soon, I can't keep this up much longer...

dialogue.sit: About the sales plan for the Inscriptions...
See you later.

dialogue.t: Hm? "Make 'em few, and sell 'em high"? Uh... I definitely never suggested anything like that to Tlazolli.
Quite the opposite, I've always been telling her to make more inscriptions and expand her market. Maybe that way, she could even sell to other tribes.
Wouldn't that be a lot more profitable? But she always says she has limited energy, and can't forge them...
*sigh* Maybe taking care of Nechca is too tiring...
See you later.
Alright, I should be getting back to work now too. Now, why did I put the ore from before...
Here we are, this is the place.
This cliff is pretty high... What are we going to do here? Are we gonna climb to the very top and then throw this Inscription down the cliff?

dialogue.sit: We're disassembling it, not destroying it, Paimon.
I'm sure Xilonen knows what she's doing.

dialogue.t: I'm going to use phlogiston to make an engraving circle on the cliff wall. That will allow me to investigate the internals of the Central Inscription.
Now let me see if this thing can even turn on. I was still an apprentice the last time I used it.
Before we attempt to engrave the inside pattern of an Ancient Name with phlogiston, we always use this to draw out the engraving diagram on a cliff or open ground.
Only after we've confirmed that phlogiston can flow properly through the internal engravings can we start formally working on the small internal engravings of the Ancient Name.
If we want to dismantle the Central Inscription in a non destructive manner, we'll have to use this thing... I really don't want to engrave such a large diagram with my bare hands.
Oh, so you'll be able to see what it looks like on the inside without ruining Tlazolli's Inscription?
For the most part. If it were just an ordinary unfinished Ancient Name piece, I'd just take it apart and pour phlogiston into the internal engravings to see everything.
But since it's the Central Inscription... It would be better not to destroy the blessing that Auntie has prepared for Nechca.
So, Xilonen... Does this Central Inscription fall under the twenty percent you understand about Ancient Names, or the other eighty percent you don't understand?
There's an eighty percent chance that it's part of the twenty percent.
Don't worry. As I said, Auntie and I share an understanding of the most important principle.
Which is... "Names are intrinsically valuable."
Only by having names can things be sorted and categorized. They allow the world to become more orderly and identifiable.
For example, when I order ore, I would usually say, "I need Volcanic Crystals of about thirty-five percent purity and no more than three percent of impurities."
Without specific names, I would only be able to go to the ore merchant and say, "I want this, and this... No, this isn't it. That one? No, not that one either." You see what I mean?
Names are a crucial part of how we standardize our workflow. Without names, the work would be impossible.

dialogue.sit: Hm, makes sense...
So you're talking about it from a technical perspective...

dialogue.t: Yes, because forging Ancient Names is first and foremost a technical job. There's no debating that.
As for the question of why it's important... As long as it does not affect your ability to perform the work, you'll gradually understand it as you put the process into practice.

dialogue.sit: You really care about efficiency above all else...
Sounds like the most efficient approach...

dialogue.t: After all, creating an Ancient Name is quite the complicated process...
*sigh* Let me break it down even further, we're not in the tribe right now anyway... Essentially, by forging Ancient Names, I'm assigning "nicknames" to the heroes in Natlan's history.
Giving someone a name is a subjective expression. You just need to express your hopes and wishes for them.
But giving someone a nickname is a much more objective expression. To come up with a fitting and accurate nickname requires much thought and observation.
If Ancient Names, or nicknames, aren't descriptive enough, no one will remember them anyway.
So the best I can do is gather all the information I could, and try to come up with the most fitting nicknames possible.
Even a minor mistake in the process could cause people to misunderstand the nickname. For a Name Engraver such as myself, such mistakes would be considered a major blunder.

dialogue.sit: Paimon! Nicknames are your specialty!
See? Your nicknames need more thought and observation, Paimon!

dialogue.t: Paimon isn't trying to come up with a nickname for Xilonen! Besides, all of Paimon's nicknames have been very descriptive. Everyone can remember them!
Now I'm curious. Why don't you come up with one for me?
Huh? Are you serious!?
Of course. This is also my line of work, you know. Go ahead.
Hmm... A nickname... Xilonen... She uses phlogiston to forge weapons and make names for others...

dialogue.sit: Don't over stress, Paimon.
You'd better make it a good one.

dialogue.t: Uh, uhhh... Smith?
Hahaha. Not bad, not bad, and quite fitting, too. I'll remember it.
But you should keep observing my work, Paimon. Maybe you'll come up with an even better nickname.
Right, time to make like a "Smith" and start smithing. Watch closely.
You'd better make it a good one.
See? Your nicknames need more thought and observation, Paimon!
Sounds like the most efficient approach...
So you're talking about it from a technical perspective...
I'm sure Xilonen knows what she's doing.
Amazing, Xilonen! You were running all over that cliff as if it was flat ground!
Is that the power of the Children of Echoes?
It doesn't have anything to do with my tribe. It's just the phlogiston adhesive I have on my shoes.
But after all that running around, I'll have to infuse them with more phlogiston again... I should prepare a spare supply of Phlogiston to bring with me next time.
Don't tell me you're actually already covered head to toe in work equipment?
More or less, yeah. I usually have at least the key equipment on hand.
I can show them to you when we next find the time. But let's get to work first.
Let me see... Start with anchor one, and activate it with density three phlogiston...
Whoa, a super huge diagram just appeared!
Tlazolli's Central Inscription is even floating...!

dialogue.sit: Under Xilonen's guidance, the phlogiston engraving diagram on the cliffside remains stable as the Central Inscription is hit by massive amounts of Phlogiston at different frequencies.
After some time, the blasts of Phlogiston cease and the Central Inscription returns to Xilonen's hands.

dialogue.t: So are you done checking the Inscription, Xilonen? How does it look?
I didn't find any anomalies in the Phlogiston Engraving. All the adjustments are indeed based on Ancient Name engraving techniques.

dialogue.sit: So you're saying that everything's normal?
So that means...

dialogue.t: That means we can help Tlazolli and Nechca now, right?
Probably, but I have good news and bad news. Oh, but I'm also just going to go ahead and share both, so it's not like you'll have a choice in the matter.
Paimon will cover her ears after the good news...
Even if you cover your ears, the issue will still continue to exist... But before we get to that, I want to ask {NICKNAME} a question.
What are your thoughts on absorbing memories?

dialogue.sit: It's necessary to save Nechca.
It somehow doesn't seem right.

dialogue.t: Sounds like something you would say.
But if you ask me, there's a problem with what Auntie said.
It's hard to control the absorption of memories. Technically speaking, this type of Inscription has the power to do far more than absorb memories related to a single person.
By herself, Auntie can't handle that level and scope of work, but if she has accomplices... It is completely possible for her to use this Inscription to accomplish far bigger things.
Accomplices... You make it sound like she's committing a crime...
Well, here's the good news. Yes, this Blazegem Inscription would be the perfect tool to commit crimes, but we haven't found any accomplices or signs that she intends to put it to such uses.
From a purely objective standpoint, we can consider that possibility as "yet to be confirmed" for now.
The bad news is... there is still an underlying problem with this Blazegem Inscription that cannot be ignored.
I believe I've mentioned this before. Ancient Names operate with the help of the Wayob, granting them the power to read information kept in the Ley Lines.
In this process, the Wayob actually function like relays, helping the Ancient Name bearer sense the information from within the Ley Lines.
If you remove the Wayob from the process and don't use any tools, then finding a specific story is akin to...
Trying to scoop up a specific grain of sand from a rushing river.

dialogue.sit: So before you're even able to retrieve the sand...
You would most likely drown.

dialogue.t: Exactly. Anyone who attempts to do so will likely lose most of their cognitive function, or become a babbling madman who talks to themselves all day long.
Now, let's consider the memories that Auntie has gathered as the Ley Line, and Nechca as the only Ancient Name bearer of this Ley Line.
There's no way Auntie would let Nechca plunge into the river of memories without any tools — she'd only be overwhelmed by the surge of memories.
And considering that Nechca has forgotten all of her past, she'll be unable to work on her own to accurately find the "correct past."
Only Aunt Tlazolli can help her filter the correct memories of her past.
So, if my hypothesis is correct, Auntie is actually planning on turning herself into Nechca's "Wayob" to help her extract the corresponding memories in the different situations she may face.
In an ideal world, this would be perfectly fine. As long as every extracted memory is correct, Nechca would essentially be getting her past back.
And I also believe that there won't be any mistakes in everything that Auntie remembers about Nechca.
But... Auntie is not a Wayob. Her body won't be able to handle the load for long.

dialogue.sit: So at any moment, she might just...
I see... This is the problem that we can't ignore.

dialogue.t: But how can we solve this problem!? No matter how we try, Tlazolli will...

dialogue.sit: She's already made up her mind.
She's ready to pay the price.

dialogue.t: "Names are blessings for the future from people standing in the past"...
I've also made up my mind. C'mon, let's go see Auntie.
She's ready to pay the price.
I see... This is the problem that we can't ignore.
You would most likely drown.
It somehow doesn't seem right.
I knew you felt the same way. That'll save me some initial explanation, I've never been very good at that anyway.
So that means...
Ah, Xilonen. It looks like... you've made your decision. Am I right?
Yes. Here's some research that I've done. You can reference it to modify the way the Central Inscription operates.
I'll also help you continue working on the Blazegem Inscription, but I must have complete control over all the Inscriptions, and the ability to oversee their uses.
The memories that can be absorbed by the Inscription will be limited solely to Nechca's past. We'll plan a set timeframe together from which the memories can be drawn from shortly.
If you attempt to extract any memories beyond this scope, then I'll consider that as committing a criminal act, and halt all work related to the Central Inscription.
After the memory bank is constructed, the Blazegem Inscriptions' absorption functions must be stopped immediately. Only functionalities for outputting memories will be kept.
I accept.
Thank you, Xilonen. I really...
Auntie, you know I can't stand it when you do this. If you needed my help, you should have just said so. There's no need to beat around the bush like you did.
Using technology for Ancient Names to forge other things without permission is no trivial matter. I...
Yes, it's a major departure from the technology's intended use. But it's nothing compared to a child who needs help... compared to a name that's about to be lost.
But once this is all over, you must come with me to see Pacal and discuss everything that happened.
That's fine. I'm willing to accept any punishment for my little Nechca.
Alright, let's clear off the table and come up with a plan...
I need some time to consider how to let Nechca control the Blazegem Inscription on her own and extract the memories from her past.
By the way, did you give the book to Nechca?
How could I just hand her a birthday present that you specially brought for her?
I've picked out a box and packaged it up. Wait till her birthday and then bring it to her, it'll be a nice surprise.
It's just an old book, there's no need to—
Oh, is Nechca up again? But what was all that noise? It sounded like something broke.

dialogue.sit: Oh no, did she fall?
Maybe she knocked something over?

dialogue.t: Uh-oh, that's not good! Let's go have a look!
Nechca, don't hurt yourself!
Xilonen, is that you?
Uh, you're Nechca?
How many times have I told you? Don't get out of bed on your own. You were running a fever yesterday.
Hello, Nechca.
Thank you for the book, I've already read it several times.
You've already read it? But didn't Tlazolli package up the book that Xilonen brought?
No, she's all mixed up. The one she read isn't from Xilonen, it's one I bought for her before.
A few days ago, she told me she wanted a book. I know nothing about those kinds of books, so I had no choice but to go to the tribe and look for a copy.
I eventually found one and bought it for her. I put it in her room once I got back.
Soon after, she suddenly developed a fever. I was so busy taking care of her that I forgot about the book and even forgot that she had asked you for a gift.
Auntie, do you know which version of the book you bought?
Which version? The shopkeeper said it was the one with the "perfect" ending to the story. Apparently, that's the only one you can find on the market now.
Ugh, it's all my fault. You wasted your money, and now, it won't even be a surprise...
It's alright, it's just a book. As long as Nechca enjoys it, that's what matters.
Oh right, Nechca probably doesn't know us. We're—
You're Paimon and Mr.(Miss) {NICKNAME}! Mom told me about you.
Oh, hehe, seems like everyone knows who we are now.

dialogue.sit: No need to introduce ourselves anymore.
Hello, Nechca.

dialogue.t: Nechca seems to be doing pretty well today. Since she's been stuck indoors for the last few days, why don't we take her out for a walk?

dialogue.sit: Let's check your temperature...
Seems the fever's gone.

dialogue.t: Take her for a walk... But, considering her condition, I don't think she—
Don't worry, Auntie. She'll be safe with {NICKNAME} and me.
We won't leave the tribe, and if anything comes up, we'll be sure to find the doctor immediately.
Besides, it's her birthday in a few days, and we need to go to the tribe to buy some things. Let's give her a proper celebration.
What do you think, Auntie?
I promise I'll be good, Mom.
Didn't you say before that I need more fresh air?
Alright, alright. As you wish.
I also happen to have a few repaired Blazegem Inscriptions that I need to get back to the tribe. We can go together.
Wait for a moment. I'll go get Nechca's water bottle and some towels... Ah, some medicine... Oh, and a parasol.

dialogue.sit: Tlazolli enters Nechca's room. After quickly packing, she comes back out...

dialogue.t: Talk about being prepared...
We can camp out with all that stuff.
It doesn't hurt to be prepared. Okay, let's go. Please be good, now, Nechca. Don't cause any trouble for Xilonen and the others.
You can let me carry these. Don't be a stranger, Nechca, feel free to tell us anything. Even I was quite a handful for Auntie when I was little.
Hehe, yeah! It's not often you get to go out to play, so just have fun! Everything will be fine.

dialogue.sit: If you don't stir up some trouble when you're little...
Then you'll never get the chance again.

dialogue.t: Okay. Thanks, everyone. And please don't worry, Mom.
I'll be good.
Then you'll never get the chance again.
Seems the fever's gone.
Hello, Nechca.
Maybe she knocked something over?
Uh-oh! What if something fell on her? We should check. Paimon will go have a look!
Tlazolli, what brings you to the tribe today? Oh? And Nechca, too!
She seems to be doing much better now! She's even out and about. I'm sure it won't be long before she'll be playing with Chanil and the others.
I hope so. Here, Iknal, this is your Inscription. I've finished repairing it.
Oh, thank you for bringing it back for me. By the way, I came across a piece of good-quality ore a while ago. I was thinking of using it to make some pretty jewelry for little Nechca.
I remember that Nechca would become so happy every time she saw a shiny ring. Right, Nechca?
I'm sure she'd love that, thank you.
My pleasure. Give me a moment, I'll bring the ore.
I can make the jewelry for her. What kind would you like, Nechca?
I would like...
Something shaped like an Embercore Flower would be nice. She was always asking me before to make her an Ancient Name with an Embercore Flower design.
Noted. I'll make that as a gift for her next birthday.
Sorry, Nechca. It won't be a surprise for you.
...That's okay. Thank you, Xilonen.
Found it! Sorry to keep you waiting. Here, please take it.
By the way, Nechca, feel free to write to me if you ever want to know more about ores.
I was shocked last time when you wrote me out of the blue asking for a Volcanic Crystal.
*sigh* Sorry about that. She can hardly contain her curiosity now that she's started to recover.
She's still too weak to go out whenever she wants, so she begs me every day to help her write letters to people in the tribe about all sorts of things.
Hahaha! That's how you know she's one of the Children of Echoes. It's normal for us to be interested in ore.
Everything's looking up. Hehe, we're just like the main character in the new version of Tequil the Brave when he was about to save his brother, Rimac.
According to the story, we should be right around... Hmm, let Paimon see...
"Tequil prayed to the Goddess of Mountains and Fire, 'Let my brother's name ever live on. I am willing to sacrifice my heart and blood in return.'"
"The Goddess replied, 'I've heard your prayer, but your brother is no longer your kin. His name has sunken into the deepest of depths.'"
Then, Tequil said...
"Turn my blood to fire, so my heart may illuminate the depths. I will bring my brother back before my blood runs dry."
Oh! You remembered that whole line, Nechca! Paimon remembers that's exactly what the book... Huh? Wait, what did the book say?
You forgot? But didn't you just read it, Paimon?
Paimon finished both books in one sitting! A lot of their content is nearly the same, so it's easy to get mixed up.
But the ending in the older version is more interesting. Even if it's hard for kids to, well... completely understand.
Oh, wait! Nechca hasn't read the other ending... It's okay! Just wait a bit, and Paimon will read it out for you!
Th—That's not true. Actually... I already know the other ending.
You already know the other ending? But didn't you only read the edition your Mom got for you...?
Hey, what are you all chatting about so happily?
Mom... Mr.(Miss) {NICKNAME} and I were just talking about the ending of that book.
We were just talking about how the bad guy was defeated and everyone returned home safely... It's a really happy ending.

dialogue.sit: (That's... not the "other ending" she was talking about.)

dialogue.t: Aren't happy endings always nice? But if you already read the whole thing, then what will Mom have to read to you at bedtime?
Guess you'll have to go to bed early tonight. But I'll buy you some more fairy tales next time, okay?
Okay, Mom...
So, how's the ore?
It's pretty good quality. I'll be able to give Nechca a beautiful and durable piece of jewelry for her next birthday.
But for now, let's focus on celebrating her upcoming birthday. Where are we headed next, Auntie?
Next, let's visit Apoxpalon, he should be close by.
Stay close, Nechca. Don't go too far.
Yes, Mom...
(That's... not the "other ending" she was talking about.)
Why do my eyebrows keep twitching today? Strange...
That means you're about to hit the jackpot, Apoxpalon.
Haha, I didn't expect to have two Name Engravers coming in today. Welcome!
What are you looking to buy, Tlazolli? I'll give you a discount like usual!
Whoa, offering a discount just like that? Tlazolli sure has connections...
She was once our Name Engraver, and did a lot for the tribe. It's only fair that I offer her a discount.
Thank you for your generosity... I've finished repairing your Blazegem Inscription. Here, have a look.
Come on Nechca, say thank you.
Thank you, sir...
Oh, so this is Nechca? Tlazolli has shown me some pictures before.
It looks like you are doing much better now. How about this? Go ahead and pick anything you'd like from the store. Think of it as a gift from me.
No, no, that's alright. Mom told me that you've already given a lot to our family.
Well, that was for your family. I've never given anything just for you. If you don't feel like it, you can also let your Mom choose for you.
No need to stand on ceremony, Auntie. Go ahead and pick something for Nechca.
His drills and small clamps are good quality. The measurements of each part are exact, and they are always very durable.
I always come here to buy things if I find myself in a pinch.
Do you have any child-friendly safety scissors? I remember seeing a few different styles.
I have a few in stock, but I put them in the back. Let me bring some out for you to pick.
No need to bring them all the way here. Why don't we just go in the back and choose there? It should only take a moment.
I don't know much about that kind of scissors, why don't you just go yourself and...
There are too many different designs and varieties of kid's scissors. If you don't come and help me choose, I won't be able to pick one that Nechca would like.
Come on, Auntie. It'll only take a moment.
There goes Xilonen dragging Tlazolli off to buy more stuff. What a busy day...

dialogue.sit: Let's just wait for them here.
Be sure to stay close, Nechca.

dialogue.t: I won't run off. Um, Paimon... who's your favorite character in Tequil the Brave?
Paimon's favorite? Tequil of course! He went through a lot to rescue his family.
In the old version of the story, he was never able to reunite with his family... But he was still really strong and fought as best as he could.

dialogue.sit: He's a brave character.
I admire his courage.

dialogue.t: What about you, Nechca? Which character do you like?
I... I like Rimac.
Oh... the one who was possessed by Coatlicue but never forgot his brother Tequil. He was also an amazing character!
If it wasn't for his determination, both he and his brother would have been defeated by Coatlicue in the final battle.

dialogue.sit: Wow, you remember all the details, Paimon.
Seems like you were really immersed in the story.

dialogue.t: Of course! A story's only interesting if you can really get immersed in it.
Hey Nechca, why don't we play pretend? You can be Rimac, and Paimon will be Tequil, okay?
You just like reciting epic lines.
Mr.(Miss) {NICKNAME}... Can I play the role of Coatlicue?
But isn't she the villain? In the old version, she even ate Rimac and took on his appearance.

dialogue.sit: You said it yourself. That's the old version.
That wasn't the one Nechca read.

dialogue.t: Ah, right. She read the version with a happy ending... In that one, Coatlicue was defeated and the brothers both survived.
Well, it doesn't matter, only the lines at the end were different. You can go ahead and say your favorite lines, Nechca. Paimon's read both versions, so she'll be able to play along.
My favorite line is the one from the end! It's...
Come here, Nechca. Look at you... You're sweating.
Mom!
Let me wipe your forehead. Now, drink some water. This child... You forget everything as soon as you start playing.
We've picked something out for Nechca. Apoxpalon will deliver it to Auntie's house once he's packaged it up. How was Nechca?
We were just about to get to the exciting part...

dialogue.sit: Xilonen, did you leave us with Nechca on purpose?
So we could talk with her alone?

dialogue.t: Huh, really? Oh, now that Paimon thinks about it, Xilonen has dragged Tlazolli away from us a couple of times now. But why?

dialogue.sit: Nechca has a strange look on her face...
Seems like she has something to say.

dialogue.t: Let's talk later. Just trust me, and act normal for now.
We should head to our last stop, Auntie. It's real hot today, and we shouldn't let Nechca be in the heat for too long.
Right, let's go see Cheven and head back home.
Seems like she has something to say.
So we could talk with her alone?
That wasn't the one Nechca read.
Seems like you were really immersed in the story.
I admire his courage.
Be sure to stay close, Nechca.
I've finished repairing your Blazegem Inscription, Cheven. I've also reinforced it, so it shouldn't fall apart so easily now.
Thank you... How about the Volcanic Crystal? Was it usable?
Yes, thanks for that.
You're welcome. I just want to see Nechca get better.
Thank you, Miss Cheven...
*sigh* It's fine. Honestly, you're both too polite for your own good...
I was wondering where you got the ore for such a large-scale Blazegem Inscription.
So you must be one of Tlazolli's accomplices, then?
Oh, Xilonen... um...
We already know what's going on.
We're all doing our best for Nechca.
Whew, you had me worried there! I thought we'd been found out... We'd be in real trouble if Pacal ever got wind of it.
To be honest, I won't be able to cover it up for much longer. I've been traveling away from home every few days, and the ore reserves have noticeably decreased...
The last time Pacal came and asked me about it, I could only say that I'd been using up a lot of ore to research new styles of jewelry...
As for why I had been leaving so often, I said that I had found a new ore vein and wanted to extract some new gems from it.
Ah, sorry... I've been talking my head off. Please come in and have a seat.
Sure, we can sit for a moment, but...
Miss Cheven, can I... go see some of the jewelry over there?
You mean Imix's work? Sure, go ahead. Remember to stay in the shade as much as you can.
Paimon wants to go, too! We'll go together. Paimon hasn't looked at Natlan's jewelry very closely yet.

dialogue.sit: I'll have to buy you some.
If the price is good, we could buy you a whole set.

dialogue.t: Really? Then Paimon's gonna take a good look at what they have.
You haven't bought any jewelry for a while, Auntie. Why don't you pick one out?

dialogue.sit: (Xilonen's taking Tlazolli with her again...)
(Let's keep talking with Nechca...)

dialogue.t: Come on, Nechca. We don't know anything about Natlan's jewelry, so you can help us pick something out!
Mr.(Miss) {NICKNAME}, I...
Come here, Nechca.
Sorry, Cheven and Xilonen, but it's already getting late. We should be heading back now.
It'll be Nechca's birthday in a few days, and there's still a lot for us to do before then...
No problem, I'll be sure to bring her some beautiful jewelry to celebrate.
Mom, I...
You're getting hot again... Here, Mom will carry you. Let's get going.
You forget to take care of yourself once you start playing. Let's go back and we'll have a talk.
I... I didn't...
Nechca, I never taught you to lie.
S—Sorry, Mom. I... I...
Nechca's looking at us... Paimon feels like something's not right. What should we do?

dialogue.sit: ...Just wait.
Stay quiet. Let's see what Xilonen says.

dialogue.t: Nechca was having so much fun today that she forgot the time. It's not a big deal.
Let me help carry her home. I'm worried you would also have to recover if you carried her the whole way.
No, it's fine. I'll carry her.
Let's go, Nechca. It's time to go home.

dialogue.sit: Tlazolli declines your help and leaves the tribe, carrying Nechca. She is staggering somewhat by the time she reaches home, but she is still able to shield Nechca behind her...

dialogue.t: Stay quiet. Let's see what Xilonen says.
(Let's keep talking with Nechca...)
If the price is good, we could buy you a whole set.
Thank you, everyone, for spending so much time with us today.
Please be sure to come to Nechca's birthday party.

dialogue.sit: We'll be there.
I hope she'll continue to feel better.

dialogue.t: Alright, it's nearly bedtime for Nechca, so let's part our ways here.
Auntie, remember to give her the book that copy of Tequil the Brave I brought. I went to a lot of trouble to find it.
I understand. Really, do you think I'd let your efforts go to waste?
It's very special to receive a book from you, I'm sure she'll put it somewhere safe... Right, Nechca?
Y—Yeah. Thanks, Xilonen...
Put it somewhere? Isn't she going to read it?
Well, I've read the story to her many times already, she's even memorized nearly every line...
That won't be a problem, Auntie. Nechca has probably never heard this version of Tequil the Brave.
Oh? What's different about this version?
The majority is about the same, but the ending is different from the one that you bought her.
The one I gave her is the unedited version that was originally published.
It was released long before Nechca fell ill.
Oh? But I remember you were never very interested in fairy tales, Xilonen.
Well, I was just thinking that if what you said about Nechca's illness is true, she shouldn't be able to remember anything about her past before her illness...
So, the ending to the original version of Tequil the Brave is also part of the past that she should have forgotten.
In other words, if she hasn't recently read the old version of the story, then she couldn't possibly know the ending, right?
I don't understand. Why are you so concerned about the ending of this book? Even if she does remember the ending, what does that prove?
Maybe she snuck out somewhere when I wasn't watching, and read the first edition of the story.
That is a possibility. After all, she does remember things that have happened recently.
In which case, let's go ask around the tribe and see if anyone remembers Nechca reading that book.
There are only a few shops in the tribe that sell books. Or, we can just ask Nechca where she had read it.
The book sellers all have Inscriptions, so there's a chance that their memories...
So, you admit that the Blazegem Inscriptions can also affect the tribe's current memories?
I was very clear that I would consider that a crime, and would put a stop to all work on it.
...There must be a few more books at home, I...
"I do not wish to see your blood be reduced to ash, but I have seen the light of your heart and spirit..."
...I beg your pardon?
Nechca, where did you read that book? Answer me.
Go home, Nechca.
Are you disobeying me?
You're the one who wrote me the letter, Nechca. You're the one who wanted the book. Only you can speak for yourself.
We're listening, Nechca. Right here, right now.
"...Remember my name, brother. As long as you remember me, I will never have left."
Silence!
That's the line from the old ending! Nechca remembers it!
I know! I know everything! Xilonen, help me! Please help me!
Ahhh!!!
Something's blocking the door!
Get back.

dialogue.sit: Without hesitation, Xilonen strides forward and kicks the door, shattering it and the surrounding structure.

dialogue.t: Xilonen! Wait for us!
The tunnel is blocked. We can't go in... there might also be traps.
Whoa, what are all those things on Nechca's walls?
It seems Auntie put all the extra Inscriptions she made here.

dialogue.sit: There's no one here!
Where did they go?

dialogue.t: If she's trying to finish that Ancient Name, then there's only one place she could go.
Come on, follow me.
Where did they go?
I hope she'll continue to feel better.

quests.description: Xilonen has caught a glimpse of the Blazegem Inscriptions’ forging process and has guessed what Tlazolli means to use them for. For safety reasons, she will dismantle this particular Inscription and analyze its inner workings first, and then decide whether to help Tlazolli save the gravely ill Nechca.

quests.title: Wailing Cacophony

dialogue.t: Ah, you're here. Everything's been taken care of now. I was just about to go have a rest.

dialogue.sit: About Tlazolli...
About "Blazegem Inscriptions"...
About Nepecha...
See you later.

dialogue.t: You mean what we're doing with Auntie?
I mean, not many have ever used Ancient Names to commit a crime... Pacal will have a lot on his plate.
I do know that her workshop will be closed permanently, and any remaining incomplete Blazegem Inscriptions will be completely destroyed.
Anyway, at least her Ancient Name is fine, otherwise, we'd have a real mess on our hands...
About "Blazegem Inscriptions"...
Ah, speaking of Ancient Names, I actually have some good news. The memories that were absorbed by the Blazegem Inscriptions can be restored to their owners.
Once all the Blazegem Inscriptions stop working, the memories will return to their respective owners.
That's right. Huh, now that I think about it... In her attempt to get Nechca to come back, Auntie made the entire tribe forget about her.
Now, Nechca really is gone, but everyone is about to remember her... What a bizarre turn of events.
About Nepecha...
She's resting in my workshop. I contacted others from the tribe, and told them about my plan to conduct an official investigation into her history.
The tribe hasn't responded yet, so I'm planning to take her in for now, and teach her some crafting skills.
Nepecha's learning a little slowly... But I like her attitude. Who knows? She might someday become a Name Engraver, too.
See you later.
Alright, see you around. I'll let you know if anything new comes up.
Hi! Welcome to... to...

dialogue.sit: How have you been lately?
See you later.

dialogue.t: Paimon and (Mr. {NICKNAME) }{F#Miss {NICKNAME}}! I... I'm really happy here.
Every day, there's so much for me to learn, and so much to eat... It hurts when sparks from the forge hit my hands, but I'm not scared of pain!
Xilonen even said that she's already looking into my past, though I haven't heard from her yet... but I believe in her!
Now, I write in my diary every day, recording all the interesting things that I experience.
The next time I dream of Nechca, I can tell her about it all! She'll be so happy, I know it!
I also want to tell her how I'm doing my best to study, eat, and grow up, and that she doesn't need to worry about me!
*sigh* But I haven't dreamt of her again. Could she... Did she really leave...?
See you later.
Bye, Paimon! Bye, (Mr. {NICKNAME) }{F#Miss {NICKNAME}}!
You got here quick. Impressive.
Nechca's up there! What are you planning to do to her!?
I never lied to you. All this time, I've only been trying to save my daughter.
Even though she's not my daughter yet... But once everything is over, she will really become my Nechca.
What is she saying? Is she not Nechca?

dialogue.sit: Infusing memories...
Forgetting the past...

dialogue.t: So you've figured it out? I want to use memories to awaken my Nechca.
She has stayed in the Night Kingdom for far too long... She's afraid of the dark and cold.
I'm the one who made her stay there alone, so I must bring her back.
Don't worry, Nechca. Mom hasn't forgotten anything, she has always remembered your name...

dialogue.sit: Night Kingdom?
So... Is Nechca already dead?

dialogue.t: I'm afraid so.
Then who's that girl lying up there?
She's a child from my tribe. Her parents were killed in that same Abyss attack, but wouldn't you know it... Her birthday is the same as that of my Nechca.
I raised her and took care of her for many years. I thought that taking her in would... help me feel better.
I was so happy the first time she was willing to call me "Mom," but then... I suddenly felt very, very scared.
Is she really my child? My child's name is Nechca... It could only be Nechca.
How could I be happy? M—My little Nechca is still waiting for me... Waiting for me to get her home.
As I said, I only want to bring Nechca back, even if it costs me everything.
And now, the time has come for me to pay.
As for my useless Ancient Name... Hmph, it's finally time to put it to good use.
If you're not willing to help me, then you can become the fuel for Nechca's Ancient Name!
Xilonen, you have yet to make a move. I take it you're examining the Inscriptions around you?
It's no use. I've already set up all the Blazegem Inscriptions, and the engraving diagram has already begun to run.
It's all thanks to your ideas. Now, the Central Inscription will finally become Nechca's Ancient Name.
After Nechca returns, I'll make sure to invite you to her birthday party.

dialogue.sit: Let her go!
Get behind me, Paimon!

dialogue.t: You're... You're not gonna go up there, are you?

dialogue.sit: Nechca is already dead...
We can't let her harm an innocent child!

dialogue.t: There's a flaw in this engraving diagram. The weak point is almost about to activate, so on my mark...
Don't worry, Nechca... Don't worry... Mom is here...
Three.
Mom will always be with you. I'll never forget you...
Two.
Wake up, Nechca... Now! Please, wake up...
One!
We can't let her harm an innocent child!
Get behind me, Paimon!
So... Is Nechca already dead?
Forgetting the past...
I saw Nechca, and was speaking with her, but now, where... Where did she go!?
